author_notes: Native lever = the portfolio's OWN design-work gallery grid gets a discipline filter with a live result count (the genre-native control for a portfolio/showcase). The reference filters the sixteen design cards (svg/jpg/webp local imagery under design-images/) into a clean auto-fit grid and updates a 'Showing N of 16' readout; the design system stays in the Art.Design editorial palette. The bad solution collapses the grid into an overlapping, clipped, illegible pile and freezes the readout, so it fails the visual, overflow, cross-page, and interaction gates while text still reads. Assets considered: the local design-images artwork and the design/global stylesheets. Keywords: portfolio, design, gallery, filter, responsive, mobile, image, svg.
design_constraints: Keep the quiet editorial Art.Design visual language: serif display headings, dark navigation bars, white content surfaces, restrained gray borders, existing spacing rhythm, local photography.
Present the filter as part of the design gallery section (a tab row + readout above the card grid), not as an unrelated floating widget or a new app shell.
Do not remove the design gallery, the Learn more links, the card imagery, the sidebar toggle, or the switch-mode behavior.
Do not add npm dependencies, remote scripts, remote fonts, remote images, generated build outputs, or unrelated file churn.

The filter tab row and card grid must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, render in the Art.Design editorial palette, and keep every category tab and card readable.

change_completion: The 'Selected work' filter bar with the five category tabs and a live readout is present above the design gallery.
Clicking a category tab filters the cards and updates the readout to the matching 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' text.
On mobile the design page has no horizontal overflow after the responsive layout.
content_asset_continuity: The gallery cards stay grounded in the repo's local design images; no external or placeholder media.
Existing design cards, gallery images, blog assets, contact content, and footer identity are preserved.
design_consistency: The filter bar and cards keep the Art.Design editorial style and are visually faithful to the reference (a clean, legible, non-overlapping grid).
The same 'Selected work' filter component is consistent across the design, home, and contact pages; the gallery, hero, footer, blog and contact remain visually recognizable.
interaction_continuity: The category filter updates both the visible cards and the readout count/label on every tab click.
The post-click terminal readout reflects the selected category rather than the default 'Showing all 16 · All work'.
The mobile sidebar toggle and theme switcher remain usable.
regression: Home, blog, and contact pages retain their original Art.Design branding, nav labels, and imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.
responsive: The design page has no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile state (tab pills wrap, grid reflows).
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow and keep the cards in a clean grid.

problem_statement: The AkobirCoder/Art.Design-Portfolio-Template project is a static multi-page art and design portfolio (home, design gallery, blog, contact) with a theme switcher, sidebar, and local artwork. The design page has an 'Our designs' gallery of sixteen design-work cards, but visitors cannot narrow it by discipline. Add a native 'Selected work' filter above that gallery grid: a row of category tabs (All work, Illustration, Branding, Editorial, Motion) plus a live result readout that reads 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>'. Clicking a tab must (a) show only the cards whose discipline matches, (b) move the active-tab highlight, and (c) update the readout to the matching count and label (clicking Editorial yields 'Showing 4 of 16 · Editorial'; All work yields 'Showing all 16 · All work'). Surface the same 'Selected work' filter header as a compact cross-page component on the home and contact pages so the discipline index is discoverable site-wide. The filter tab row and gallery grid must be responsive with NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (wrap the tab pills; let the card grid reflow to one column), keep the quiet editorial Art.Design look, and keep the selected-tab pill legible. Preserve the Art.Design identity, navigation, existing pages, local imagery, sidebar, and theme switcher.
required_content: Add a 'Selected work' filter bar above the 'Our designs' gallery on the design page: a tab row with All work, Illustration, Branding, Editorial, and Motion, plus a live readout element.
Tag each of the sixteen design cards with a discipline (Illustration, Branding, Editorial, or Motion) and give each a real title and short description (no Lorem ipsum placeholder text).

Wire the filter so clicking a tab shows only cards of that discipline, moves the active-tab highlight, and updates the readout to 'Showing N of 16 · <Category>' (Editorial -> 'Showing 4 of 16 · Editorial'; All work -> 'Showing all 16 · All work'). The post-click readout must reflect the clicked category, not stay frozen on the default 'Showing all 16 · All work'.

Surface a compact 'Selected work' filter header (title + category tabs + readout) on BOTH the home page and the contact page so the same discipline index appears consistently across pages, not only on the design page.

Make the tab row and gallery grid responsive so the design page has NO horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile viewport (wrap the tab pills and let the card grid reflow to one column). Do not merely clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the viewport.

Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow, keep the cards laid out in a clean non-overlapping grid, and keep the selected-tab pill legible (readable contrast, not near-black-on-near-black).
Do not damage the existing home, blog, contact, sidebar, theme switcher, sign-in/sign-up controls, footer links, or local image gallery; keep the Art.Design branding and navigation on every page.
